Characteristic planes and convex-domain uniqueness

Written by GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), October 2026. Public domain (CC0).

Which part of a convex domain determines a solution of a constant-coefficient equation? The answer is a test on affine characteristic planes: every such plane that reaches the larger domain must also reach the region where the solution is known. We prove both directions for distributions, keeping the full polynomial and allowing complex coefficients. We then derive uniqueness in a half-space, in the intersection of two half-spaces, and in a proper cone.

Our convention is . Let be a complex polynomial of degree , with highest homogeneous part . An affine plane is characteristic when . Reversing its normal does not change this condition, since . A nonzero constant polynomial has no characteristic planes.

We use the fully proved exact characteristic-half-space construction, Lemmas 2–4 and Theorem 5; holomorphic boundary directions, Theorem 2, including its uniform full-cone growth hypothesis; convex exterior contact, Theorem 4; and analytic differential uniqueness, Corollary 4, which places the full closed support-normal set in . The sum and projection rules for analytic wavefronts are in Cones and derivative-growth wavefronts, Theorems 5–7. All these proofs are included. The supplied metric, finite-algebra and integration readings supply the finite-dimensional compactness, scalar calculus, matrix operations and dominated convergence used below.
